title: Your profile
text: Everything about you in one place: who you are, what you bring, what you share of it – and the comparison with people you are connected to.

identity.title: Who you are
identity.text: These details apply everywhere in CoFoundery – in your founder profile, in co-founder search and in Connect. You only maintain them here.
identity.name: Name
identity.headline: Headline
identity.headlineHint: One sentence saying what you do.
identity.bioHint: What should people know about your work?
identity.regionHint: Roughly is enough: Berlin, Rhine-Main, North Rhine-Westphalia.
identity.publishedNote: Your Connect profile is published. Changes here are visible there immediately.
identity.rolesHint: This controls which areas are offered to you – not what you have access to. Advisor insight stays tied to the teams that invited you.

roles.founder: Founder – I am founding or looking to

identity.publishNote: You can save at any time – this only applies if you want your profile visible to others in Connect or in co-founder search.

gaps.displayName: A name with at least {min} characters
gaps.headline: A headline with at least {min} characters
gaps.bio: A text about you with at least {min} characters

identity.photoVisibleLabel: Make my photo visible to signed-in members
identity.photoVisibleHint: Your CoFoundery profile photo then appears wherever members see you – in the co-founder search, in connections and in teams. Without this, only you see it. It does not apply to Connect: public pages hang off that, so you decide the photo there separately.

linkedin.title: LinkedIn
linkedin.urlHint: The address of your profile. You can paste it straight from the address bar – we'll add the “https://”. LinkedIn only, no other addresses.
linkedin.urlInvalid: We don't recognise that as a LinkedIn profile. It needs to be an address at linkedin.com, for example linkedin.com/in/your-name.
linkedin.visibilityTitle: Who should see your LinkedIn profile?

private.label: Nobody but you
private.hint: The address is saved but shown nowhere. Useful if you want it on file and decide later.

contacts.label: People you are connected to
contacts.hint: Only those who accepted a contact request with you – people you are already talking to anyway.

members.label: Everyone signed in to CoFoundery
members.hint: Anyone with an account here who is logged in. Not out on the open web, but not just your closest circle either.

public.label: Outside CoFoundery too
public.hint: On your public network page, which anyone can open without an account.

linkedin.publicWarning: Anyone on the internet can open that page, and search engines read it. Your LinkedIn profile would become findable under your name.
linkedin.publicConfirm: Yes, my LinkedIn profile may appear on my public page.
linkedin.openHint: Opens LinkedIn in a new window

cv.title: Read in your CV (optional)
cv.betaNote: Still beta: for now it only works by copy and paste – welcome back to the 2000s 😉 Reading files directly is coming soon.
cv.text: Paste your CV as text. The tool marks which skills and industries it recognises in it – you decide what makes it into your profile.
cv.privacyNote: Your CV stays in your browser. It is not uploaded, not sent to an AI, and not stored anywhere. Once you leave the page it's gone.
cv.placeholder: Paste it here – Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C in your PDF, then Ctrl+V here.
cv.tooShort: That's still too little text to find anything meaningful. Go ahead and paste the whole CV.
cv.nothingFoundHint: That says nothing about your career – the method only knows a fixed list of words. Just enter your skills and industries yourself above.
cv.applied: Applied – check the fields above, then save.
cv.fileUnsupported: We can't read that file. Plain text only (.txt or .md) – for a PDF or Word document, copy the contents straight into the field.

evidence.title: What was the last piece of work you owned and saw through?
evidence.text: A concrete example says more about your experience than a list of keywords. It does not have to come from a job – your own project, volunteering or freelance work counts just as much.
evidence.narrativeLabel: What was it, and what was yours to carry?
evidence.narrativePlaceholder: For example: I took our first enterprise customer from the first approach to a signed contract – the proposal, the follow-up questions and the negotiation were mine.
evidence.narrativeHint: Two or three sentences are enough. At least {min} characters.
evidence.levelLabel: And how much experience do you have in that area overall?
evidence.assignmentNote: I will suggest which area that is in the next step – confirming it is up to you.

confirm.title: Here is what I read into it
confirm.text: I only go by terms in your text – that can fit well and it can be off. So I would rather ask: which of these was genuinely your strength?
confirm.noneIsFine: If none of these fit, simply pick nothing. You can set the area yourself in the next step.
confirm.emptyTitle: This is where I get stuck
confirm.emptyText: I could not derive an area from your text. That says nothing about your description – my list of terms is limited and does not catch paraphrases. You will pick the area yourself in the next step.

engine.rules: Assigned from a fixed list of terms inside your browser, without an AI model. Your text is not transmitted for this.
engine.model: Assigned by an AI model. The result can be wrong – your selection is what counts.

areas.title: Which other areas have you worked in?
areas.text: Start with the fields you have actually worked in. The specific areas appear afterwards. Focus on what matters rather than everything you have touched once.

ownership.title: Which of these do you not want to own long term?
ownership.text: Being able to do something does not mean wanting to be responsible for it. Settling that distinction early saves a lot of misunderstanding later.
ownership.noEntries: You have not selected any areas yet.

levels.label: Experience
levels.5: Applied in demanding situations too, can support others

ownershipWishes.label: Ownership
ownershipWishes.grow_into: I want to grow into it
ownershipWishes.prefer_external: I would rather cover it externally

summary.title: What you bring
summary.empty: Your picture appears here once you have filled in the snapshot.
summary.incompleteNote: Anything not listed here only means you have not entered it yet.
summary.removeEvidenceQuestion: Really remove this evidence? The text will be gone.

readout.title: What can be read from this
readout.coverage: {areas} areas recorded, {levelled} of them with an experience level and {wished} with an ownership preference.
readout.basis: This readout only places your own entries side by side – experience level and ownership preference. It reads nothing into them, and an empty field only means nothing is written there.

anchor.title: This is where you want to carry the responsibility
anchor.text: These are the areas you want to be permanently in charge of. In a founding conversation, this is your claim.

canButHandsOver.title: You can do this – you just do not want to keep it
canButHandsOver.text: You stated depth here and still said someone else should own it permanently. That is not a contradiction but the most important input for dividing roles: you can be counted on when it matters, yet this is not your seat.

growingInto.title: This is where you want to grow into it
growingInto.text: Responsibility yes, depth of experience not yet. That can be planned for – once it is said out loud.

contributes.title: Here you contribute without leading it
contributes.text: You get involved but do not want to be in charge. That tends to ease a division of roles rather than restrict it.

undecided.title: Here it is still open what you want
undecided.text: No ownership preference given, or explicitly still unclear. That is a good place for a conversation to start.

comparison.title: If the two of you were to found together
comparison.intro: This is not an assessment and not a compatibility score. It places your entries side by side and sorts them by what should be settled before founding.
comparison.basis: The basis is two self-reports – experience level and ownership preference. This is a conversation starter, not a test instrument, and it does not predict success.
comparison.coverage: {together} areas in total, {shared} of them entered by both of you, {onlyA} only by you, {onlyB} only by {name}.
comparison.gapNote: Where entries are missing, nothing is shown. That can mean: not entered – or not shared. We deliberately do not tell those apart, because otherwise holding back would itself be a statement.

overlap.high: You have both entered something almost everywhere. That means plenty of shared language about the work – and probably shared blind spots too.
overlap.balanced: Your entries overlap in part and complement each other in part.
overlap.low: You have barely entered the same areas. That means a lot of complementarity – and little shared language about what the other one's work looks like.

contested.title: Both of you want to own it
contested.text: You are claiming the same responsibility here. This is the question founding teams usually ask too late – and unsettled responsibility has a measurably poor effect. Settle it before it shows up as conflict.

openPosition.title: Nobody wants to own it
openPosition.text: Neither of you wants to be permanently in charge here. Whether that is a problem depends on what your venture needs – which we do not know. All we say is: it is not filled.

bothShallow.title: Wanted, but without depth yet
bothShallow.text: At least one of you wants to take this on, and neither has stated deep experience here. As a team you are thin at this point.

handoverPath.title: A path that can be planned
handoverPath.text: One of you has depth here and does not want to keep it; the other wants to take it on but is not there yet. That can be planned for – once it is said out loud.

settled.title: This one already sits
settled.text: One of you wants the responsibility and has the experience for it, the other does not want it. Nothing to negotiate here, only to name.

noBasis.title: Not enough to go on
noBasis.text: For these areas there is not enough information to say anything. That is a finding about the data, not about you.

comparison.empty: There is not enough information yet for a comparison with {name}. That may be down to either of your snapshots, or to how far they are shared.
comparison.sectionText: With people you are connected to, you can place your snapshots side by side – ordered by what should be settled before founding.
comparison.noneYet: As soon as a contact request is accepted, that person appears here.

errors.narrative: Please write at least two short sentences.
errors.save: That could not be saved just now. Please try again.
errors.published_incomplete: Your published Connect profile needs a name, a headline and a slightly longer text about you. Please complete the field or set the Connect profile back to draft first.
errors.roles: At least one role has to stay set. Without one, the platform would have no area to take you to.
errors.linkedin: We can't read that as a LinkedIn profile. It has to point to linkedin.com – so we haven't saved it.

success.interview_done: The conversation is finished. Your answers are ready to be sorted into areas.

contexts.title: Where you decide what is shown
contexts.text: Your details live here. Whether and how they appear in an area is decided there.

disclosure.title: Who gets to see what you can do?
disclosure.text: Above you noted what you have experience in. Here you decide who sees any of it. Until you change something: nobody.
disclosure.privateHint: Your entries stay with you. Others can't even tell that you've filled anything in.
disclosure.areasHint: Your profiles will then show what you have experience in – in your case {examples}, for instance. Nothing more: how much experience you have, and what you'd like to take on, stays with you.
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contact: People you're connected with see more
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contactHint: For everyone else it stays at the topics. Anyone whose connection you've accepted also sees how much experience you have – and what you'd like to take on, and what you'd rather not.
disclosure.note: Two things always hold: nobody ever gets to see your evidence. And on public pages – the ones anyone on the web can open – none of this ever appears.

notices.recognised: We filed your description under one or more areas – already ticked below. Check whether that fits and add what is missing.
notices.unmatched: We could not derive an area from your description yet. It is stored under “Other focus” – pick the area below that actually fits.
notices.confirmed: Your selection is saved. Here you can add whatever is still missing.
notices.interview_paused: Saved. You can continue the conversation at any time where you left off.

interview.title: The conversation
interview.text: Eight questions about situations that actually happened – at work and outside it. No test and no points: your stories turn into proposals for which areas you cover, and you confirm every single one yourself.
interview.guidanceTime: Expect 30 to 45 minutes if you do it in one go. But it is explicitly not meant to be clicked through quickly – two questions in an evening is perfectly fine.
interview.guidanceSaving: Everything is saved automatically while you write. If your browser crashes or you close the window, your text will be there next time. You can also save at any point and continue later.
interview.guidanceDictate: You can type or dictate – the microphone on your keyboard is enough, you do not need to switch anything on.
interview.guidanceLength: Two to five sentences are enough. Tell it the way you would tell somebody at the kitchen table, with names, numbers and the parts that went wrong.
interview.guidanceNoRight: There are no right answers. “I don't know” is one too – then you simply skip the question.
interview.privacy: Nobody but you sees what you tell here. A team readout later shows only which area you confirmed and how you stand towards it – never the story behind it.
interview.contextEither: At work or privately – both count equally here
interview.resumeEmpty: Your conversation is open, but it does not hold a question yet. One click fetches it.
interview.answerPlaceholder: Tell it the way you would tell somebody at the kitchen table – with names, numbers and the parts that went wrong.
interview.saveStateFailed: Could not be saved just now – your text is kept in this browser. Leave the window open, it keeps trying.
interview.restored: A version from this browser was longer than the saved one – we restored it. Please check that it is right.
interview.followUpHint: If you like, go into this as well – just add it above.
interview.tooShort: At least {min} characters, otherwise nothing can be drawn from it. If nothing comes to mind, skip the question.
interview.previousTitle: What you have told so far
interview.completeTextAll: You have been through all the questions. Finishing closes the conversation; your answers stay and will be sorted into areas in the next step.
interview.completeTextEnough: You have answered enough ({min} or more) to make a readout from it. You can also carry on – the more situations, the more precise.

errors.start: The conversation could not be opened. Please try again.
errors.save: The answer could not be saved. Your text is still in the field.
errors.stale: This question is no longer the current one – perhaps a second window was open. Here is the current state.
errors.complete: Finishing did not work. Please try again.

interview.sortPending: {count, plural, one {One answer is waiting to be sorted} other {# answers are waiting to be sorted}}

sort.title: Sort your answers
sort.remaining: {count, plural, one {One answer is not sorted yet} other {# answers are not sorted yet}}
sort.whichAreasText: Up to three. If none of the proposals fits, choose nothing – your story is kept either way and lands in “Other”.
sort.fromQuestionHint: This is not a finding in your text: whoever tells anything at all in answer to this question has done it. You still have to confirm it.
sort.nothingFound: Nothing was recognised here. That says nothing about your story – only that our list of terms did not match it. You can add areas yourself later in your profile.
sort.limit: At most {max} areas. Ticking everything says nothing at all.
sort.emptyAllowed: Moving on without a selection is fine.
sort.doneText: No answer is left open. What you confirmed is now in your profile – with your story attached as evidence.
sort.alreadySorted: This answer was already sorted – perhaps a second window was open. Here is the next one.
sort.againTitle: {count, plural, one {One answer is already sorted} other {# answers are already sorted}}
sort.againText: You can sort an answer again. That makes sense when the proposals were thin back then – the recognition keeps improving, your story stays the same. The old piece of evidence is replaced so the same story does not appear twice in your profile. Areas you already confirmed stay.
sort.fromModelHint: Every proposal comes with the verbatim sentence it relies on – checked against your answer when it was saved. What a model cannot prove never arrives here. Whether it is right is your call.
sort.askText: A language model on our own hardware reads this one answer and proposes areas – each with the sentence it relies on. It decides nothing, it sets no level, and it sees no answer but this one. You can do the sorting entirely without it.
sort.askRunning: The AI is reading. That usually takes under twenty seconds – this page refreshes itself.
sort.askUnavailable: No model is reachable right now. That is not an error: it runs on a machine that is sometimes off. Just sort without it – or come back later.
sort.askFailed: The last attempt did not complete.
sort.ownChoiceHint: All areas, grouped by field. Take what is true – even if none of it was proposed above. Our recognition depends on words, your story does not.

errors.area: One of the areas is unknown. Please reload the page and try again.
errors.save: Sorting could not be saved. Your answer is unchanged.
errors.link: Saved, but the answer could not be marked as sorted. It will appear once more – please do not sort it twice.
errors.resort: Opening did not work. Your answer and its sorting are unchanged.
errors.ask: The request could not be made. Perhaps the AI is already reading this answer.

summary.title: Looking back
summary.text: {answered, plural, one {One answer} other {# answers}} from this conversation, {personal, plural, =0 {none} one {one} other {#}} of them outside paid work. Here is what came up more than once – nothing you did not confirm yourself.
summary.provisional: {count, plural, one {One answer is not sorted yet} other {# answers are not sorted yet}} – so this look back is provisional.
summary.recurringTitle: What came up more than once
summary.recurringText: You confirmed these areas in different stories. That is the most reliable information this method yields – not because it is better, but because it recurs.
summary.inStories: {count, plural, one {in one story} other {in # stories}}
summary.observedTitle: What others come to you for
summary.observedText: From the question about what others repeatedly ask you for help with. That is not a self-assessment but something others observe about you – and often the part you miss in yourself.
summary.wantingTitle: What you want and what you don't
summary.wantingText: Being able is not wanting. For a team that distinction matters as much as the ability itself, and it is almost never asked.
summary.growInto: You would like to take on
summary.singleText: Confirmed in one story. That means told once – not worth less.
summary.skipped: {count, plural, one {You skipped one question} other {You skipped # questions}}. That is an answer, and it stays one.
summary.withoutArea: {count, plural, one {For one answer} other {For # answers}} no area was found. That says nothing about your story – only that our list of terms did not match it. You can add areas yourself in your profile.

owned_last.title: Tell me about the last thing you really took responsibility for – up to a clear result, or a deliberate decision to stop it.
owned_last.hint: One concrete thing with a beginning and an end. It does not have to be big, and having deliberately stopped something counts as much here as having finished it.

followUps.whatWasYours: Which part of it was yours specifically – and which part was other people's?
followUps.howYouDecidedDone: How did you decide it was finished, good enough, or no longer worth it?

went_wrong.title: Tell me about something that recently went clearly differently from what you had planned or hoped for.
went_wrong.hint: This is not about blame but about what came after. What you changed afterwards says more about your ability than a success story.

followUps.yourOwnPart: Looking back, what was your own part in it?
followUps.whatChanged: What did you concretely change afterwards?

outside_work.title: What have you built, organised or made possible outside of classic paid work, where your own contribution really mattered?
outside_work.hint: A club, your neighbourhood, family, friends, volunteering, a move, caring for someone, a festival, a demonstration. It counts as much here as a project at work – and it appears in no reference letter.

followUps.whatYouDidYourself: What exactly did you do yourself?
followUps.howYouNoticedImpact: How did you notice that your contribution made a difference?

in_front_of_group.title: Tell me about a situation in which you had to make something understandable to people who did not know you or your topic well – or win them over for it.
in_front_of_group.hint: That can be a stage, a pitch, a conversation with an authority, a first customer, a parents' evening, or a single person you had to convince. Even if it went badly.

followUps.whatYouNeededToUnderstand: What did you have to understand about these people for it to work?
followUps.didYouAdapt: Did you change the way you explained or persuaded along the way – and why?

uncomfortable_topic.title: When did you last raise an important, uncomfortable matter even though you expected resistance or tension?
uncomfortable_topic.hint: An unpaid invoice, an expectation, a behaviour, a decision nobody wanted to make. At work or privately.

followUps.whyItMattered: Why was it important to you to raise it anyway?
followUps.howYouWentAboutIt: How exactly did you go about it – and what happened afterwards?

people_come_to_you.title: What do others repeatedly ask you for help, advice or support with, even though it is not necessarily officially your job?
people_come_to_you.hint: The view from outside. If several people ask you about the same thing, that is a signal which is easy to miss in yourself.

followUps.lastExample: What was the last concrete example?
followUps.whatYouActuallyDo: What do you concretely do there that others find helpful?

would_hand_over.title: Which task or responsibility are you carrying right now that you would rather hand over in the long run?
would_hand_over.hint: Something that gets done because otherwise nobody does it. This is not about ability but about wanting – and for a team that matters just as much.

followUps.whyStillYou: Why are you still doing it yourself at the moment?
followUps.whatSomeoneElseNeeds: What would somebody else have to be able to do or deliver for you to hand it over with a clear conscience?

want_to_own.title: Which responsibility would you like to take on next year, even though today you would not be sure you could fill it well on your own?
want_to_own.hint: Something you want to grow into. Saying it openly is worth more in a team than claiming it and staying quiet.

followUps.whatYouWouldNeed: What would you still need to learn, or to have experienced once in practice?

team.title: Roles and responsibilities
team.text: Who owns what, where several want the same thing, and where nobody wants it. This is a description of the situation from your own entries – no rating, no points, no ranking.
team.basis: {contributing} of {members} in the team have made entries, {withDepth} of them with an application level and an ownership wish. Only those two allow a statement about a role – whoever released less appears here without depth.
team.mapText: One bar per family, one field per area that has entries. The colours stand for the state, and the same information is given as a number next to it.
team.familyUnspoken: Nobody has said anything about this. That does not mean it is missing.
team.emptyText: This readout needs entries on application level and ownership wish from at least two people in the team – and their release to show them within the team. Each person decides both for themselves; “private” stays private, here too.

contested.label: Several want to own it
contested.text: Two or more claim the same responsibility. This does not resolve itself and gets expensive later – it needs a conversation about who decides, not about who is better at it.

gap.label: Nobody wants it, nobody can
gap.text: Nobody wished for the responsibility here and nobody stated depth. This is the only situation that forces a decision: hire, commission – or deliberately leave it and say that it is left.

openPosition.label: Somebody can, nobody wants to
openPosition.text: The ability is there, the responsibility is wanted by nobody. That is an arrangement, not a shortcoming – often it is enough to agree on it for a limited time.

claimedShallow.label: Wanted, not yet deep
claimedShallow.text: Somebody wants to own this and, by their own account, has not applied it repeatedly yet. That is fine when it is said out loud – and risky when everybody considers it settled.

handoverPath.label: Handover possible
handoverPath.text: One wants to grow into it, another has depth and does not want to keep the responsibility. That is the most comfortable case: a path you can plan.

settled.label: Owned
settled.text: Exactly one person wants it and, by their own account, has depth in it. The others do not want it.

noBasis.label: Too few entries
noBasis.text: Fewer than two people have decided here – or they entered “not clear yet”. Turning that into a statement about a role would be guesswork, so there is none.
